survey: Object: an inflatable beach ball resting on sand. Main parts: (1) a spherical body made of six vertical gores, alternating colored and white. From left to right you can see red, white, blue (front center), white and green; the sixth gore is hidden behind. (2) A purple round cap at the top pole, tilted slightly toward the camera. The gores all narrow to meet the cap's rim. (3) The bottom pole is on the hidden underside. The gores are widest near the visible equator in the lower part of the ball, and the side gores (red, green) look narrower because they turn away from the camera. The ball sits on the sand. It flattens slightly where it touches the ground and casts a contact shadow on the right, so it is clearly resting rather than floating. The gores meet in clean seams, with no overlaps, gaps or melting. The count of six alternating gores matches a real beach ball, and its round shape holds up.
